name: Benard Convection Cells
desc: Rayleigh-Benard convection seen from above, integrated as the Swift-Hohenberg equation the real thing reduces to near onset — a fluid heated from below organizes into a honeycomb of hexagonal convection cells with hot rising cores and cool sinking rims, or into rolls, or into spiral-defect chaos where grain boundaries glide and defects nucleate and annihilate without ever settling; false-colour thermal, planetary magma crust, hammered bronze relief, drafting blueprint, or sumi ink.

energy.doc: brightness + colour gain across the hot cores and cool rims

scale.doc: magnification into a sub-region of the convection cell — guaranteed visible change

speed.doc: simulation rate — how fast cells form, glide and reorganize (0.2 still evolves)

density.doc: thermal fluctuation + the uneven-heating ramp that nucleates defects and grain boundaries (low = serene lattice, high = restless chaos)

rayleigh.doc: Rayleigh number above threshold: 0 = quiescent conduction, mid = clean cells, 1 = hard turbulent convection

hexa.doc: up-down symmetry breaking — 0 selects stripe ROLLS, 1 selects the iconic HEXAGONAL Benard cells

relief.doc: how hard the cells are lit into rounded pseudo-3D convection domes

hue.doc: primary hue anchoring the hot end of the thermal ramp

x.doc: horizontal pan of the magnified region

y.doc: vertical pan of the magnified region

style.doc: aesthetic: false-colour thermal cells / dark magma crust with molten inter-cell cracks / hammered bronze relief (light only) / drafting blueprint iso-lines / sumi ink wash

seed.doc: deterministic seed for the initial fluctuation
